comment: A block written as a VALUE rather than as a bare JSX attribute: `const panel = @( … )` outside JSX, and `css={@( … )}` inside the braces JSX already has for an expression. The second exists because of a limit nothing here can lift — an editor stops consulting injections once it enters a tag's attribute list, so a bare block gets no colours unless it is the first attribute on the tag name's own line.

value.comment: The lookbehind mirrors the compiler's scanner, which requires a `=` before the block. Permitting a bare `{` instead would swallow a parenthesised decorator written on the same line as a class's opening brace — measured, `class C { @(dec) m() {} }` lost its `dec`.
